record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Existence of bisection degree threshold gb(s,t)
record.original_question: For given integers s and t, does there exist an integer l such that every graph with minimum degree at least l has a bisection (S, T) satisfying delta(G[S]) >= s and delta(G[T]) >= t? If such l exists, what is the smallest such threshold gb(s,t)?

evidence.quote: Recall that a bisection is a bipartition of which the two subsets have size as equal as possible.

Can we have an analogue of Stiebitz’s theorem in bisections? In other words, for given integers s and t, is there an integer l such that every graph with minimum degree at least l has a bisection (S, T ) with δ(G[S]) ≥ s and δ(G[T ]) ≥ t? If such a constant does exist, we use gb(s, t) to denote the smallest one[45].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A bisection of G is an ordered partition (S,T) of V into two sets whose sizes differ by at most 1. For a subset U⊆V, let G[U] denote the subgraph induced by U, and let δ(H) denote the minimum degree of a graph H. For nonnegative integers s and t, decide whether there exists an integer ℓ=ℓ(s,t) with the following property: every graph G with δ(G)≥ℓ admits a bisection (S,T) such that δ(G[S])≥s and δ(G[T])≥t. If such an integer ℓ exists, determine the smallest such ℓ, denoted gb(s,t). (This is the bisection analogue of Stiebitz's theorem, which asserts that minimum degree at least s+t+1 suffices to guarantee a (not necessarily balanced) bipartition with the analogous induced minimum-degree conditions.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2025) establishes that a threshold function for the bisection analogue of Stiebitz's theorem exists: every graph with minimum degree at least some f(k)=O(k) admits a bisection in which each induced part has minimum degree at least k. Thus existence of gb(s,t) is established (at least when s=t and asymptotically), but the exact value of gb(s,t) remains undetermined, so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Bisections of graphs under degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a function f(k)=O(k) such that every graph with minimum degree at least f(k) admits a bisection where every vertex has ≥k neighbors in its own part.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a linear threshold for the bisection analogue of Stiebitz's theorem is established, but exact thresholds remain open.

status_evidence.title: Stiebitz, Discrete Mathematics (1987)
status_evidence.snippet: Every graph with minimum degree at least s+t+1 has a vertex partition into parts inducing subgraphs of minimum degree at least s and t.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Stiebitz theorem provides the non-balanced analogue used to motivate gb(s,t).
